internal_decisions: parse_date checks the text with re.fullmatch on ASCII [0-9] digits before calling date.fromisoformat, so trailing newlines, whitespace and non-ASCII digits are rejected

plan: Baseline: tests (31) and acceptance (19) all pass.
Contracts/integration: ledger -> balances -> settle flow sums to zero; failed add after a valid add changes nothing (green).
Edge cases: odd amount and date strings, split sum property (green).
Defects D1 and D2 are medium/low, so their tests stay red on purpose.
Non-functional, regression: discarded; no persistence or prior code, and the architecture names no security or performance needs.

defects.section: 6 (Ledger.add: a failed add changes nothing; balances is defined for every ledger)
defects.repro: Ledger().add('2026-01-01','Ann','5.00',[]) succeeds. Every later balances() call then raises ValueError('parts must be at least 1: 0') from split(cents, 0). The ledger is permanently unusable.
defects.fix: In _clean_participants (or add), raise ValueError when participants is empty, before the expense is stored.
defects.if_skipped: One bad add makes balances() raise on every later call, so the ledger can't be used and there's no way to remove the expense.

defects.repro: month_end(date(9999,12,5)) raises ValueError('year 10000 is out of range'). months_between(date(9999,12,1), date.max) raises the same error. The contract expects 9999-12-31 and [(2026-..)] clipped periods.
defects.fix: In _first_of_next_month, compute month_end without building year+1, for example via calendar.monthrange. Stop the months_between loop at end's month.
defects.if_skipped: Only dates in year 9999 fail, with an uninformative error.

gaps: The contract does not say whether an empty participants list should be rejected. D1 treats it as a defect because balances() breaks afterwards.
Non-str arguments (for example None as an amount) raise AttributeError rather than ValueError. The contract doesn't cover them, so I did not test them.

advisory.problem: AC-009: the ValueError case for start > end only checks the one example, where the months differ. An implementation that checks only the month would pass it. Wrong implementations are still unlikely to pass the other assertions.
advisory.evidence: A check like `if (start.year, start.month) > (end.year, end.month)` passes. The same-month case with start > end is not tested.

advisory.problem: AC-011: the invalid cases are all checked in one ledger, and balances() == {} is checked only at the end. That is enough to catch partial recording. Date and amount parse errors, such as a bad date text, are not covered. The criterion does not list them.
advisory.evidence: None needed. This is a minor coverage gap that the criterion itself allows.
